---
title: "Size and book-to-market claims"
---

Table 7 takes the market fit of [Estimation](estimation.qmd) as given
and asks what the model says about the top and bottom quintiles sorted
by size and by book-to-market. Preferences, consumption dynamics, and
the states extracted from the market's price-dividend ratio and the
risk-free rate stay at the market estimates. Each portfolio gets its
own cash-flow vector: the mean $\mu_j$, the loading $\phi_j$ on
expected growth, the loading $\varphi_j$ on volatility, and the
correlation $\varrho_j$ of its own shock with the consumption shock.
The moments are the paper's: mean and volatility of dividend growth,
its correlation with consumption growth, the risk premium, return
volatility, mean and volatility of the price-dividend ratio, and the
market beta.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
from great_tables import GT

from geap.lrr.estimation import (
    estimate_bky,
    estimate_table7_claims,
    load_annual,
    load_cross_section,
    table7_panel_a,
    table7_panel_b,
)

KIKU_GT = dict(table_background_color="transparent", table_font_size="0.92rem",
               heading_title_font_size="1.05rem", heading_subtitle_font_size="0.85rem",
               source_notes_font_size="0.8rem", column_labels_font_weight="bold",
               data_row_padding="4px")

panel = load_annual()
portfolios = load_cross_section()
```

## Panel A: cash-flow parameters and risk premia

```{python}
fit = estimate_bky(panel)
claims = estimate_table7_claims(portfolios, market_params=fit.params, h=fit.h)
a = table7_panel_a(claims, portfolios, fit.params, fit.h)
params = a[["claim", "mu", "mu_paper", "mu_paper_se", "phi", "phi_paper", "phi_paper_se",
            "phi_sigma", "phi_sigma_paper", "phi_sigma_paper_se", "rho", "rho_paper", "rho_paper_se"]]
(
    GT(params)
    .tab_header(title="Table 7, Panel A. Cash-flow parameters by portfolio")
    .tab_spanner(label="mu_j", columns=["mu", "mu_paper", "mu_paper_se"])
    .tab_spanner(label="phi_j", columns=["phi", "phi_paper", "phi_paper_se"])
    .tab_spanner(label="varphi_j", columns=["phi_sigma", "phi_sigma_paper", "phi_sigma_paper_se"])
    .tab_spanner(label="rho_j", columns=["rho", "rho_paper", "rho_paper_se"])
    .cols_label(claim="", mu="ours", mu_paper="paper", mu_paper_se="SE",
                phi="ours", phi_paper="paper", phi_paper_se="SE",
                phi_sigma="ours", phi_sigma_paper="paper", phi_sigma_paper_se="SE",
                rho="ours", rho_paper="paper", rho_paper_se="SE")
    .fmt_number(columns=["mu", "mu_paper", "mu_paper_se"], decimals=4)
    .fmt_number(columns=["phi", "phi_paper", "phi_paper_se", "phi_sigma", "phi_sigma_paper",
                         "phi_sigma_paper_se", "rho", "rho_paper", "rho_paper_se"], decimals=2)
    .tab_source_note("mu_j is per decision period. Paper: BKY (2016) Table 7 Panel A, with its bootstrap SEs.")
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

```{python}
premia = a[["claim", "premium_data", "premium_data_paper", "premium_model", "premium_model_paper"]]
(
    GT(premia)
    .tab_header(title="Table 7, Panel A. Risk premia, percent a year")
    .tab_spanner(label="Data", columns=["premium_data", "premium_data_paper"])
    .tab_spanner(label="Model", columns=["premium_model", "premium_model_paper"])
    .cols_label(claim="", premium_data="ours", premium_data_paper="paper",
                premium_model="ours", premium_model_paper="paper")
    .fmt_number(columns=["premium_data", "premium_data_paper", "premium_model", "premium_model_paper"], decimals=2)
    .tab_source_note("Data: mean real return of the Ken French quintile legs, 1930 to 2015. Paper: BKY (2016) Table 7 Panel A.")
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

## Panel B: CAPM betas and alphas

The model's betas come from a long simulation of the four claims and
the market on one path of shocks. Alphas are the model premium of the
spread minus beta times the market premium, in percent a year.

```{python}
b = table7_panel_b(claims, fit.params, fit.h, portfolios, panel, years=2000, seed=1)
(
    GT(b)
    .tab_header(title="Table 7, Panel B. CAPM implications")
    .tab_spanner(label="beta, data", columns=["beta_data", "beta_data_paper"])
    .tab_spanner(label="beta, model", columns=["beta_model", "beta_model_paper"])
    .tab_spanner(label="alpha, data (%)", columns=["alpha_data", "alpha_data_paper"])
    .tab_spanner(label="alpha, model (%)", columns=["alpha_model", "alpha_model_paper"])
    .cols_label(spread="", beta_data="ours", beta_data_paper="paper", beta_model="ours",
                beta_model_paper="paper", alpha_data="ours", alpha_data_paper="paper",
                alpha_model="ours", alpha_model_paper="paper")
    .fmt_number(columns=[c for c in b.columns if c != "spread"], decimals=2)
    .tab_source_note("Paper: BKY (2016) Table 7 Panel B.")
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

::: {.firewall}
Every "paper" column is quoted from Bansal, Kiku, and Yaron (2016),
Table 7. The portfolio panel is the Ken French size and book-to-market
lowest and highest quintiles, with and without dividends, deflated by
the BLS CPI. The second stage is a weighted minimum-distance fit on
the paper's moment list with the states extracted from the market,
not the paper's joint GMM, and it reports no standard errors. The
loadings and premia land near the paper's. The model beta of small
minus large does not: the simulated beta stays about half the printed
0.86, even with the market beta among the fitted moments, so the
model's size alpha is smaller than the paper's. `NUMBERS.md` lists the
open caveats.
:::
